text: Were the courses taken by other students because they filled up before he could register?
Were his course selections removed from his registration by an administrative action?
Did he lose his courses because of a computer or system error?
Did he miss the course selection deadline, causing the courses to be cleared?
Did he personally drop or cancel his courses (perhaps accidentally)?
Did "all of my courses were gone" mean the courses were no longer available/offered (e.g., cancelled) rather than that he lost his enrollment?
Was the student's course list emptied because his account/eligibility status changed—for example, he was no longer considered an enrolled student?
Did he see the empty course list because he was looking at the wrong place—wrong semester, wrong program, or wrong system view—while his actual courses were still enrolled?
Were the courses released/gone because the course selection period had not yet opened, and the empty list was simply before his enrollment window?
Was the student's course selection rejected because he failed to pay tuition or fees, so his enrollment was voided?
Did a friend or another person use his account and drop or swap his courses?
Did the courses disappear from view because the student was checking after the add/drop period, so the system only displays currently active courses—not a loss of enrollment?
Did the university cancel or suspend classes (e.g., due to a typhoon, holiday, or emergency), so that "all courses were gone" means no classes were held that evening?
Did the student accidentally delete his own course selections while using the system?
Is the student able to re-add the courses, meaning they were never actually lost—only the displayed list was temporarily empty due to a lag/refresh issue?
Did the student lose the courses he had planned or wanted to take because they filled up—i.e., all the courses on his wish list became full in one evening?
Were the courses "gone" because the student's laptop/phone was stolen or his password was compromised?
Does "all of my courses were gone" refer to physical course materials (notes, textbooks, files) disappearing rather than his course registrations?
Was the course selection done through a bidding/points system, and he spent or lost all his bid points in that one evening, leaving him unable to secure any courses?
Did the student's courses get removed because a hold or block was placed on his student account (e.g., library fines, disciplinary hold, advising requirement)?
Was the student trying to enroll in courses but they were all already full when his enrollment appointment/window opened?
Did the student physically leave (was absent from) all his classes one evening, so "all my courses were gone" means he was gone from them?
Had the student already completed/graduated from all his courses, so he had no courses left to choose?
Was the cause related to a change of major/curriculum, such that his previously planned courses no longer applied to his program?
Were the courses "gone" because the enrollment website/app simply shut down or became inaccessible that evening?
Did the student himself cause the courses to disappear by using the system incorrectly—for example, searching with the wrong filters or navigating to an empty results page?
Were the courses gone because they were all scheduled in a time slot that conflicted with another course, and the system removed them for the clash?
Is the "evening" significant because course selection at HKU opens at a specific time (e.g., a midnight or evening release), and all spots were taken within that evening?
Did the student drop all his courses himself because he decided to take a gap year, withdraw, or change his plans?
Did the student sleep through / oversleep, so in the morning his courses were gone because the deadline had passed while he was asleep?
Were the courses "gone" because the course list he was viewing was for a different semester/year than the one he needed?
Did the student lose his courses because he was on a study-abroad/exchange program, and his home-university course registrations were voided during that period?
Were the courses "gone" because the student was checking a paper printout or notice that was simply outdated, while his online enrollment was fine?
Did the student's courses get removed because he was dismissed, suspended, or had his offer/registration revoked by the university?
Is there wordplay on "courses" — for example, does it mean dishes/meals (courses of a meal) rather than classes?
Did the student eat all his meal courses (dishes) in one evening?
Does "choose my courses" here mean selecting meal courses at a dining hall or restaurant, and "gone" means someone ate/served/removed them?
Were the meal courses gone because the dining hall ran out of food that evening?
Did the student himself eat the meal courses that evening, so they were gone because he consumed them?
Does "University of Hong Kong" relate to a dining setting, such as a canteen or a formal dinner/banquet there?

Is the twist that the student is actually at a university dining event (e.g., a formal hall dinner or catered event), where "choosing courses" means picking dishes from a menu, and the dishes ran out before he chose?
Are the "courses" dishes that vanished because they were cleared away (e.g., plates removed) rather than eaten?
Did someone clear away the dishes before the student could eat/choose them, thinking the meal was over?
Did the courses disappear from the online course catalog/listing because the enrollment system was displaying them as unavailable for his selection window?
Did the student consume alcohol/heavy drinking that evening, such that "all my courses were gone" is a figure of speech for being very drunk or losing track?
Does "gone" refer to the evening itself passing—i.e., the evening went by quickly—rather than the courses disappearing?
Are the "courses" a multi-course meal served at a university event, and "gone in one evening" means the food was eaten/finished at the event (by others, not him)?
Are the "courses" a multi-course meal served at a university event/dinner?
Was the food eaten/finished by other attendees at the event, so the courses were gone before the student got to choose or eat them?
Was the student late to the event, so by the time he arrived the meal courses had already been served and cleared?
Were the "courses" gone because they were never actually served—e.g., the event was cancelled or the meal was called off that evening?
Did the meal courses disappear because they were eaten (consumed) rather than cleared away or cancelled?
Did the student mistake something else for "his courses"—for example, he was reading a menu whose dishes were sold out, but this was at a restaurant, not the university?
Are the "courses" dishes that were still there but simply not available to him—for example, they were reserved for other guests or he was not entitled to them?
Did the student eat his meal courses, so they disappeared because HE ate them (the opposite of my earlier hypothesis, which the host may have been ambiguous about)?
Were the courses removed/cleared by staff as a normal end-of-meal routine while the student was still expecting to eat them?
Did an animal (e.g., a pet or bird) eat or take the food, causing the courses to disappear?
Is the disappearance of the courses a consequence of the student's own action other than eating—for example, he dropped them or spilled them?
Did the student drop or knock over the dishes, so the food was gone (spilled) before he could eat it?
Did the student cause the courses to disappear by accidentally throwing them away or discarding them (e.g., binning his food or clearing his own tray)?
Did the student lose his course *registrations* through his own action—such as submitting or confirming a wrong form or clicking a withdrawal option?
Was the student's own action something like leaving the food unattended or uncovered, after which it was removed/spoiled?
Did the student fail to secure a place in any of his desired classes because they filled up before he registered?
Is the disappearance of the courses caused by the student's own action of *cancelling or unenrolling* them—that is, he dropped them himself?
Was the student's own action simply that he temporarily left his seat/table (e.g., went to the restroom), and during that time his food was cleared?
Did the student accidentally choose *nothing* on the selection form—submitting a blank or incomplete order/registration—so he ended up with no courses?
Does the puzzle hinge on "courses" meaning classes (university course enrollment), not meal dishes?
Did the student himself send the courses back / return the dishes to the kitchen (e.g., rejecting them)?
Did the student's own action involve *sharing* the courses—giving his food away to others—so they were gone from his plate?
Was the disappearance of the meal courses caused solely by the student (with no other person or process involved)?
Did a staff member clear the plates because the student appeared finished—for example, he placed his cutlery together or set his napkin down to signal he was done?
